# S6: Transition replay fallback for invalid direct Jira transitions

## Context / Problem
A Jira workflow may forbid the DIRECT end-state transition rebar wants (e.g.
`open -> done` when only `open -> in_progress -> done` is allowed); the outbound sync
then fails and the ticket drifts. Status flows `update_one` ->
`client.update_issue(status=...)` -> `transition_issue_by_name`. Cloud:
`AcliClient.transition_issue_by_name` (`adapters/jira/acli.py:489`) lists available
transitions, POSTs one hop, raises `RuntimeError` when none reach the target
(`acli.py:536`) or `urllib.error.HTTPError` on a non-2xx POST. DC:
`JiraDataCenterTransport.transition_issue_by_name` (`adapters/jira_datacenter/
_issues.py:229`) -> `transition_to_status` -> `resolve_transition`, which raises
**`ValueError`** when no transition reaches the target (`transitions.py:104`); the
illegal-from-current-state case is `IllegalTransitionError`, a `ValueError` subclass
deliberately NOT an `HTTPError` (`transitions.py:33-36`). The direct path runs ONE hop
and gives up; `_update_one_scalar_update` (`dispatch_one.py:583`) turns the failure
into comment-fallback + drift (`result=None`).

Replay mirrors rebar's REAL recorded status hops to reach the end state via allowed
intermediate hops. Self-healing (inventing hops rebar never took) is OUT of scope.

## Approach
1. **Data source — recorded hops (grounded, event-sourced).** Every transition
   appends an append-only `STATUS` event `<tracker>/<local_id>/<ts>-STATUS.json`,
   written by `rebar._commands.txn` (`txn.py` ~L330):
   `data={"status":<target>,"current_status":<from>,...}`. Files sort by filename =
   chronological — the ordering `reduce_ticket` replays in (`reducer/_api.py:138`) and
   `txn._parent_status_uuid` uses (`txn.py:105`). NEW helper
   `recorded_status_hops(local_id, tracker) -> list[str]` globs `*-STATUS.json`, sorts
   by filename, returns the ordered `data["status"]` targets FORWARD-mapped local->Jira
   via `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` (`value_maps.py:78-86`). The sequence lives entirely in
   **Jira-name space**, e.g. `["To Do","In Progress","Done"]`.

2. **Ambiguity-free resume — NO inverse map.** `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` is NON-INJECTIVE
   (`value_maps.py:78-86`: `In Progress` <- {in_progress,blocked}; `Done` <-
   {closed,cancelled,deleted}), so it has no inverse. We NEVER invert it. Read the
   issue's current status via the existing required member `client.get_issue(remote_id)`,
   take `fields.status.name` (a Jira NAME), and match it DIRECTLY against the
   forward-mapped hop list from (1) — all comparison in Jira-name space. Tie-break: on
   multiple positional matches anchor on the LAST (highest index; Jira is at its
   most-recently-synced state) and replay the hops AFTER it. No positional match ->
   abort (see 4). No local status is ever reconstructed from a Jira name.

3. **Replay uses ONLY the existing seam.** No list-available-transitions method exists;
   the required member is `TicketTransport.transition_issue_by_name(remote_id,
   target_status)` (`_backend.py:250`). **No new transport method.** Replay calls it
   once per remaining Jira-name hop, in order; each call re-fetches the now-current
   per-issue transitions and executes the next legal hop.

4. **Failure mode — grounded, covers BOTH implementors.** The per-transition
   required-field abort is DROPPED (no field metadata is fetched and the transport has
   no method for it). Replay aborts if ANY hop raises the UNION of what both named
   implementors raise: `RuntimeError` (acli, `acli.py:536`), `ValueError` (DC
   no-transition AND its `IllegalTransitionError` subclass, `transitions.py:33,104`),
   `urllib.error.HTTPError`/`JiraAPIError`/`BackendHTTPError` (a 400, incl. an
   un-fillable required field on the POST). On abort it falls through to the EXISTING
   comment-fallback + drift arm (`dispatch_one.py:622`, `result=None`). No partial hop
   is retried.

5. **Call-chain threading (explicit).** The replay call site is inside
   `_update_one_scalar_update` (`dispatch_one.py:583`), invoked by `update_one`
   (`:413`) at `:470-472`.
   - `client`: ALREADY the first parameter of both `update_one` and
     `_update_one_scalar_update` — in scope at the site, no change.
   - `local_id`: `update_one` holds it as `mutation.get("local_id")` (`mutation` in
     scope; cf. `:128`, `:470`). `_update_one_scalar_update` does NOT receive it today,
     so ADD one parameter `local_id: str | None` to `_update_one_scalar_update` and pass
     `mutation.get("local_id")` from the `:470-472` call. This is the ONLY signature
     change; the two `update_one` callers (`apply_handlers.py:347`,
     `apply_outbound.py:161`) are UNTOUCHED — `mutation` already flows into `update_one`.
   - `tracker` / `repo_root`: NOT threaded. `replay_transition` derives the store via
     `config.tracker_dir(reconciler_repo_root())` — `reconciler_repo_root()`
     (`config.py:512`) is the reconciler-owned root this module ALREADY self-resolves
     (`dispatch_one.py:156-158`, `:275-277`); `config.tracker_dir(root)`
     (`config.py:135`) applies the store's config precedence. No `repo_root`/`tracker`
     parameter is added anywhere.
   Wiring: in the widened failure catch (union in 4), call `replay_transition(client,
   issue_key, local_id, target_status)` FIRST (it self-resolves the tracker); only if it
   returns False does the current comment-fallback run. Falsy `local_id` -> skip replay,
   comment-fallback as today.

## Scope
- NEW `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/transition_replay.py`:
  `recorded_status_hops(local_id, tracker)` and `replay_transition(client, remote_id,
  local_id, target_status)` (resolves the tracker via
  `config.tracker_dir(reconciler_repo_root())`). Keeps `dispatch_one.py` (**678 LOC**;
  hard cap 800 — `AGENTS.md` module-size policy) under the cap.
- EDIT `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py`: (a) add `local_id: str |
  None` parameter to `_update_one_scalar_update` and pass `mutation.get("local_id")` at
  the `:470-472` call; (b) widen the except in `_update_one_scalar_update` to the union
  in (4) and call `replay_transition` before comment-fallback; (c) import the helper. No
  change to `update_one`'s signature or to its two callers.
- No transport/protocol change; no new required member.

## Testing
NEW `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_transition_replay.py`: fake Cloud and DC
transports recording `transition_issue_by_name` calls (DC fake raising
`ValueError`/`IllegalTransitionError`, Cloud fake raising `RuntimeError`), an on-disk
tracker of `*-STATUS.json` events, and `reconciler_repo_root`/`tracker_dir` pointed at it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `test_replay_walks_recorded_intermediate_hops` — hops open->in_progress->closed,
  workflow rejecting the direct hop: transport receives `transition_issue_by_name(
  "In Progress")` then `("Done")`, in order.
- [ ] `test_replay_resume_point_matches_in_jira_name_space` — `get_issue` reporting
  "In Progress" replays only "Done"; resume index found WITHOUT inverting the map.
- [ ] `test_replay_duplicate_jira_name_anchors_on_last_occurrence` — "In Progress" at
  two positions resumes after the LAST match.
- [ ] `test_replay_never_invents_unrecorded_hops` — a hop absent from the recorded
  sequence is never sent.
- [ ] `test_replay_aborts_and_drifts_on_illegal_hop` — PARAMETRIZED over BOTH backends:
  a mid-chain hop raising `RuntimeError` (Cloud) AND one raising
  `IllegalTransitionError`/`ValueError` (DC) each abort replay and run comment-fallback
  (`result is None`, no further hops).
- [ ] `test_recorded_status_hops_orders_by_filename` — targets returned in filename
  order, forward-mapped to Jira names.
- [ ] `test_replay_aborts_when_current_status_not_in_sequence` — a Jira status name
  absent from the hop list aborts to drift.
- [ ] `test_replay_skipped_when_local_id_absent` — a mutation with no `local_id` skips
  replay and behaves as today (comment-fallback + drift).

Test tier: unit
